title: terraform block without required_version
msg: terraform block has no required_version — whatever CLI the runner happens to have will run this root module, including a major that rewrites the state file.
fix: Add required_version = "~> 1.9" (or your tested range) inside the terraform block.

title: provider configured with no required_providers block
msg: provider "{name}" is configured but this file declares no required_providers block — Terraform falls back to the implied hashicorp/{name} address at the newest release.
fix: Add a required_providers block with an explicit source and version for {name}.

title: provider missing from required_providers
msg: provider "{name}" is configured but is not listed in required_providers — Terraform assumes registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/{name}, unversioned.
fix: Add {name} = { source = "...", version = "~> X.Y" } to required_providers.

title: required_providers entry without source
msg: required_providers.{name} has no source — Terraform assumes the hashicorp/ namespace, which is the wrong publisher for most third-party providers.

title: required_providers entry without version
msg: required_providers.{name} has no version constraint — a clean terraform init takes the newest release unless .terraform.lock.hcl is committed alongside it.

title: provider constraint with no upper bound
msg: required_providers.{name} = "{value}" has no upper bound — the next provider major is inside this constraint.
fix: Use the pessimistic operator, e.g. "~> 5.62", or add an explicit < bound.

title: wildcard provider constraint
msg: required_providers.{name} = "{value}" matches every release ever published, in both directions.
fix: Replace the wildcard with a bounded constraint such as "~> 3.6".

title: constraint tracking a 0.x provider
msg: required_providers.{name} = "{value}" tracks a 0.x provider — below 1.0 the minor digit is allowed to break, and ~> only holds the last digit.
fix: Pin the minor too, e.g. "~> 0.9.0", or pin exactly until the provider reaches 1.0.

title: required_version with no upper bound
msg: required_version = "{value}" has no upper bound — a new CLI major can upgrade the state file, after which every older CLI refuses to read it.

title: s3 backend still locking through DynamoDB
msg: The s3 backend uses dynamodb_table — Terraform 1.10 added native S3 state locking via use_lockfile and marks the DynamoDB locking path deprecated.
fix: Set use_lockfile = true, migrate, then drop dynamodb_table.

title: registry module without version
msg: module "{name}" pulls registry source "{value}" with no version argument — terraform init takes the newest published module, on every clean checkout.
fix: Add version = "~> X.Y" to the module block.

title: git module source without ?ref=
msg: module "{name}" points at a git source with no ?ref= — it tracks whatever the default branch HEAD is at init time.
fix: Append ?ref=<tag or commit SHA> to the source.

title: git module pinned to a branch name
msg: module "{name}" pins ?ref={value} — a branch name moves, so this is not a pin.
fix: Use a release tag or a full commit SHA instead of a branch.

title: module fetched over plain http
msg: module "{name}" is fetched over plain http:// — the module body is not authenticated in transit.
fix: Use https:// or a git:: source over SSH.
